header: # MOCK-APPLY node fixture `hashman_lock_standin` (HQ 2026-10-27 ruling 7) for user_lock (harness title p8testuser).
# user_lock runs hashman's `pp_auth.py lock <user>` on the Puppet master (required_base hashman_base, whose database
# lives in the master's code tree). Its ruled guard (upstream_defects.md user_lock) reads the user's entry in
# hashes.pp, so the user must exist in hashman's database for the define to be idempotent. On a real master the user
# was created through hashman beforehand; here the fixture supplies ONE fake database entry for p8testuser (the fixture
# hash `$6$p8testsalt$...`, never a real user's), added by a seeding exec before user_lock's exec, only if absent
# (hashman_base declares hashes.pp itself with replace => no, so the fixture cannot declare the file).
# (2026-11-17, HQ ruling 2: the code-tree directory left this fixture; the agent package ships it.)
# Behaviour (a locked user refused by pp_auth/the web interface on a master) is NOT verified by a GREEN with it.
# Lifted by: a master-role node whose hashman database holds the user (no nodes.yml kind yet; HQ batch-5 ruling 6; HQ 2026-11-17 ruling 2)
resources: exec[p8test seed p8testuser into the hashman database]
node_fixture.scope_evidence: hashman_lock_standin: file /usr/local/sbin/p8test-seed-hashman-user (root 0755 script that appends one fake entry $p8testuser_pwd_hash = '$6$p8testsalt$p8testfixturehash' to hashman's hashes.pp only if absent) and exec 'p8test seed p8testuser into the hashman database' (runs it, guarded by unless grep for the entry, require the script + Class[hashman_base], before Exec[user_lock_p8testuser]). Both serve exactly the stated stand-in (one fake DB entry for the harness title p8testuser); neither declares nor alters any attribute of the class's exec user_lock_p8testuser or hashman_base's hashes.pp resource (only an ordering edge)
